content: The fecal-oral route is a mode of transmission for numerous diseases, occurring when fecal particles from one host are introduced into the mouth of another potential host. This pathway is also referred to as the oral-fecal route or the orofecal route. Typically, there are intermediate steps involved in this transmission process, which may include several stages. One of the most common causes of transmission via the fecal-oral route is the consumption of water that has been contaminated with feces and inadequately treated before drinking. Similarly, food that has been handled in the presence of fecal matter can also serve as a vehicle for disease transmission. Poorly managed sewage systems or inadequate sewage treatment further contribute to the spread of diseases through this route. Additionally, insufficient or absent hand hygiene after handling feces or objects contaminated with fecal matter significantly increases the risk of transmission. Certain sexual practices, such as anal-oral sex or coprophilia, can also facilitate the spread of diseases through the fecal-oral route. These behaviors involve direct or indirect contact with fecal matter, thereby increasing the likelihood of disease transmission.
